import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 966

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/966](https://www.erdosproblems.com/966)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées
  Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
-/

namespace Erdos966

/--
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

Erdős [Er75b] reported that 'Spencer has recently shown that such a sequence exists', but gives
no reference.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos966.lean"]
theorem erdos_966 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → 2 ≤ r → ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAPOfLengthFree (k + 1) ∧
      ∀ coloring : A → Fin r, ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k := by
  sorry

end Erdos966

reformulations.difference: Nontrivial progressions are encoded by exact set cardinality rather than an explicit positive-common-difference condition. Also, the cited formal proof colors all of ℕ, whereas this declaration colors the subtype A.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each permitted length m ≥ 2, a zero difference produces at most one distinct element, contradicting ENat.card = m. Conversely, a positive difference makes i ↦ a + i*d injective on Fin m, giving exactly m terms. Coloring A is equivalent here to coloring ℕ: restrict a global coloring, or extend a coloring of A by any fixed color outside A, available since r ≥ 2. The per-witness equivalence is proved as Review966.witness_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Paul Erdős, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory, Astérisque 24–25 (1975), pp. 295–310; definition of A(k) on pp. 295–296 and §IV(i), p. 306. https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1975__24-25__295_0.pdf
Local repository: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/AP/Basic.lean; definitions Set.IsAPOfLengthWith, Set.IsAPOfLength, Set.IsAPOfLengthFree, and ContainsMonoAPofLength.
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Finite.lean and Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean; ENat.card and set-cardinality semantics.
Local repository: FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and FormalConjecturesUtil/Attributes/Basic.lean; answer and status/proof annotation semantics.
review.notes: The sole declaration agrees with [Er75b] §IV(i), including its note that Spencer established a positive answer. Checked quantifiers, conjunctions, lengths, color count, answer polarity, and boundary cases. Scratch proofs exclude empty-set and zero-step witnesses and verify k = r = 2 with A = {0,1,3}; finite exhaustive computations agree. The linked proof compiled successfully, and /workspace/review/verified-link.lean derives the exact repository statement from it. Both depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, supporting the formal_proof record. Source-access limitation: the current erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so their latest remarks could not be checked. The original cited paper and linked formal proof were available and sufficient to verify the declaration.
